population: the 74 confirmed support gaps from C37, re-validated against roll collapse in C39
purpose: supply objective 4's missing search term. The charter ranks by rows x is-engine-gap x changes-tree-pricing-at-decision-margins, and only the third term was unmeasured.

margin_1_lethality.why_this_margin: KO vs no-KO is the largest single value discontinuity a gen3 tree has
margin_1_lethality.a_miscoding_i_caught: My first pass reported 1 inversion (1.4%) and I was about to adjudicate the whole bucket as search-irrelevant on it. The categories were wrong: 'sim survives but SOME engine branch KOs' fell through into the 'neither KOs' bucket because the test demanded EVERY branch KO. Fixed, the true figure is 16 -- an order of magnitude larger, and it reverses the adjudication.
margin_1_lethality.the_direction_matters_more_than_the_coun: 15 of the 16 are the engine believing it can KO where the simulator says the defender survives. That is the over-optimistic direction -- premature commits into 'guaranteed' KOs that were not -- which is the bias flagged for post-C27 evaluation. It is still present in the residual support gaps.

margin_2_n_hit_KO_threshold.why_this_margin: a median 44% magnitude error should move how many hits it takes to kill, which is what a tree prices when deciding to stay in, switch, or set up

adjudication.verdict: the engine-gap bucket DOES change tree pricing at decision margins. The third term of the ranking formula is not zero.
adjudication.evidence: 21.6% lethality inversion and 75.7% n-hit-KO threshold shift, both measured offline on the confirmed-unreachable population
adjudication.era: derived on engine fingerprint 51d56b3f (53 patches) and the post-C35 readout; must be re-derived on any fingerprint or readout change
adjudication.what_i_would_have_written_instead: On the miscoded lethality figure alone I would have adjudicated this bucket as real but search-irrelevant and closed it. That adjudication would have been wrong and would have closed the highest-impact open work in the program.

ranked_target_for_objective_4.first: the 15 over-optimistic lethality inversions -- smallest row count but the sharpest margin and the known-harmful direction
ranked_target_for_objective_4.then: the 56 n-hit-KO threshold shifts, which subsume most of the rest
ranked_target_for_objective_4.still_required_before_any_patch: a registered prediction with the tactics-suite regression gate, and a mechanism. C39 established the bucket is heterogeneous -- half engine-smaller, a quarter larger, a quarter bracketing -- so there is no single fix, and the 15 inversions need their own mechanism diagnosis before a patch can be scoped.

does_not_reach_a_pass: no code changed; unattributed stays at 485
CORRECTED_BY: reports/c41_lethality_claim_retraction.json -- the lethality/over-optimism claim is RETRACTED. 'Some branch KOs' vs 'no branch KOs' are not mirror conditions; on symmetric thresholds the asymmetry is 5 vs 1 at n=6 (not significant) with a Brier score of 0.066. The n-hit-KO threshold shift (56 of 74) stands and is the real search impact.
